title: Growth in abstract steps
cap: Exact values of n, n squared, and two to the n at selected input lengths; exponential versus polynomial growth, not clock time.
tex:
\(\begin{array}{r|r|r|r}
n& n&n^2&2^n\\ \hline
4&4&16&16\\
8&8&64&256\\
12&12&144&4096\\
16&16&256&65536\\
20&20&400&1048576
\end{array}\)\par\medskip
On a base-two log scale: \(\log_2(n^2)=2\log_2 n\), \(\log_2(2^n)=n\).\par
\(\begin{array}{r|rrrr}
n&4&8&16&32\\ \hline
\log_2(n^2)&4&6&8&10\\
\log_2(2^n)&4&8&16&32
\end{array}\)
\par These are exact step-count functions, not universal lower bounds.

title: Reachability by breadth-first layers
cap: The directed graph a to b to c to d and a to e. BFS layers from a are {a}, {b,e}, {c}, {d}; from e only e is reached.
tex:
\(\begin{array}{ccccccc}
a&\longrightarrow& b&\longrightarrow& c&\longrightarrow&d\\
\downarrow&&&&&&\\[-2pt]
e&&&&&&
\end{array}\)\par\medskip
\(\begin{array}{c|cccc}
\text{distance from }a&0&1&2&3\\ \hline
\text{frontier}&\{a\}&\{b,e\}&\{c\}&\{d\}
\end{array}\)\par
Start at \(e\): no outgoing edge. Reachability \(e\to a\) is false.\par
The BFS core processes each vertex once and scans its outgoing edges.

title: A clause-occurrence clique witness
cap: Three clause rows contain distinct literal occurrences. The compatibility table records every cross-clause edge, and the three c occurrences form a witness clique.
tex:
\(\Phi=(a\lor b\lor c)\land(\neg a\lor b\lor c)
\land(a\lor\neg b\lor c)\)\par
\(\begin{array}{c|ccc}
C_1&a_1&b_1&\boxed{c_1}\\
C_2&\neg a_2&b_2&\boxed{c_2}\\
C_3&a_3&\neg b_3&\boxed{c_3}
\end{array}\)\par
Rows are clauses; columns are occurrence positions. Join every pair in
different rows except complementary literals.\par
\(\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{row pair}&\text{missing cross-row edges}\\\hline
1,2&(a_1,\neg a_2)\\
1,3&(b_1,\neg b_3)\\
2,3&(\neg a_2,a_3),(b_2,\neg b_3)
\end{array}\)\par
\(\boxed{c_1\longleftrightarrow c_2\longleftrightarrow c_3
\longleftrightarrow c_1}\)\quad witness triangle.
\par No same-row edge exists. All other cross-row pairs are edges.

title: Witnesses for SAT and non-tautology
cap: The same formula is true when b is one and false when both bits are zero. One witness proves SAT membership; another refutes TAUT membership. No separation is claimed.
tex:
\(\theta=(a\lor b)\land(\neg a\lor b)\)\par
\(\begin{array}{c|c|l}
(a,b)&\theta&\text{meaning}\\\hline
(0,1)&1&\text{witness for SAT}\\
(0,0)&0&\text{witness for non-TAUT}
\end{array}\)\par\medskip
\(\boxed{\exists w:\theta(w)=1}\qquad
\boxed{\exists w:\theta(w)=0}\)\par
SAT and non-TAUT have existential certificates; TAUT asks for
\(\forall w:\theta(w)=1\).\par
\(P\subseteq NP\cap coNP\); equality questions are unresolved.

title: A conditional search algorithm
cap: A hypothetical SAT decider selects a feasible positive or negative literal at each step. The class inclusion chain only identifies P versus EXPTIME as a proved strict endpoint.
tex:
Assume a polynomial-time SAT decider \(D\) and a satisfiable formula \(F\).\par
\(\begin{array}{c}
D(F\land x_i)\\
\swarrow\quad\quad\searrow\\
\text{YES}\qquad\qquad \text{NO}\\
F\gets F\land x_i\quad F\gets F\land\neg x_i\\
\downarrow\qquad\qquad\downarrow\\
\multicolumn{1}{c}{\text{continue with a satisfiable restricted formula}}
\end{array}\)\par
One choice per distinct variable yields a satisfying witness.\par
\(P\subseteq NP\subseteq PH\subseteq PSPACE\subseteq EXPTIME\).\par
\(P\ne EXPTIME\) is proved; \(P=NP\) is open.

title: Quantifier order and dependency
cap: For equality of two bits, choosing x before all y fails, while responding with x equal to y succeeds. The polynomial hierarchy uses bounded quantifier blocks.
tex:
\(\begin{array}{c|cc}
x=y&y=0&y=1\\\hline
x=0&1&0\\
x=1&0&1
\end{array}\)\par
\(\exists x\,\forall y\ (x=y)\): no row is all ones; false.\par
\(\forall y\,\exists x\ (x=y)\): every column has a one; true.\par
The choice \(x=y\) depends on the previously chosen \(y\).\par
\(\Sigma_0^P=\Pi_0^P=P,\quad\Sigma_1^P=NP,\quad\Pi_1^P=coNP.\)\par
Each bounded-alternation level lies in PH; strictness not asserted.

title: Winning responses in a quantified game
cap: For all x there exists y with x=y, universal AND branches choose x and existential OR branches choose y=x. Depth-first evaluation reuses the current path.
tex:
\(\forall x\,\exists y\ (x=y)\)\par
\(\begin{array}{c}
\text{AND: choose }x\\
\swarrow\quad\quad\searrow\\
x=0\qquad x=1\\
\text{OR}\qquad\text{OR}\\
\swarrow\ \searrow\quad\swarrow\ \searrow\\
\boxed{1}\ \ 0\qquad 0\ \ \boxed{1}\\[-1pt]
y=0\quad y=1\quad y=0\quad y=1
\end{array}\)\par
Boxes mark the winning responses, one per universal branch.\par
A depth-first decider retains only the current path and control state,
not the entire strategy tree. Printing a strategy is another task.

title: An exponential execution with small space
cap: Three-bit counter cycles through eight states and returns to zero. General k-bit counter uses k bits for 2^k increments. The output itself is trivial.
tex:
\(\begin{array}{cccc}
000&\to001&\to010&\to011\\
&&&\downarrow\\
111&\leftarrow110&\leftarrow101&\leftarrow100\\
\downarrow&&&\\
000&&&
\end{array}\)\par
Eight increments modulo \(2^3\), three counter bits.\par
General \(k\): \(2^k\) increments, \(k\) counter bits plus control.\par
The returned value is always zero; no intrinsic time lower bound follows.\par
\(P\subseteq PSPACE\subseteq EXPTIME,\quad P\ne EXPTIME.\)
